title: Show me the best UI kit you made 100% with AI.
author: jablaza
selftext:
Hey guys, solo ai dev here. Iam wondering how far did you manage to get just with using AI to create UI/HUD for your games. 

For me each new project is getting stuck on this topic - games are playable, looking good but i always get stuck on the UI and it takes hours and hours for me to make it look perfect. 

Therefore i wonder if anyone has a good workflow to share with the community, to prevent your UI look like AI slop. Thanks in advance!

comments.author: dank_summers
comments.body: I'd say put in a placeholder to start, then build out your world and find a style. Then comeback and build a UI to fit the world and feed it reference images of what you like

replies.author: jablaza
replies.body: Yesh i do this, but it never ends up looking good. Could you share images of what you have achieved?

comments.author: DigitalDustChan
comments.body:
Would you pay $50 for the solution?

I'm making a plugin for Unity that will greatly improve how the AI makes UI by forcing it to be creative when it counts.

replies.author: jablaza
replies.body: Yea i would. If the result is real good looking UI

comments.author: jamurai
comments.body: What model are you using? GPT hasn’t been great for me but Opus 5.5 creates amazing UIs. Provide it with direction, have it research, and have it mock it up with a claude artifact webpage first. Review iterate and then implement. I’ve gone through probably 5 ui redesign to end up with something I’m now really happy with

replies.author: jamurai
replies.body: It’d be more helpful to see screenshots of your current UI and workflow. Happy to give some critique or pointers if you do

comments.author: svekkxor
comments.body:
It's basically the first thing I built even before game systems. It's one of the hardest things to change later and I wanted to have some kind of guaranteed consistency. Drew a lot of inspiration from design systems in modern spa's, even though I'm working in godot.

Now agents are forced to use or improve the components that exist and it helps a ton. Each time I add a new panel imI can be relatively sure its somewhat consistent. And if it's not: "did you use existing design system components?" -> oops no, and they selfcorrect 😅

replies.author: jablaza
replies.body: Can you share some screenshots? I ussually use claude design for some ideas but it never looks good. It always looks like AI slop ui, even when i provide reference images of what i want and then itterate multiple times. Never happy woth the result

comments.author: Kingnorik
comments.body: Just prompt some mock images. Take parts that you like. It takes time, hours and hours.

replies.author: jablaza
replies.body: If i use claude design, looks like AI slop even tho i provide refference images. If i use opus 5.5 or even fable, result is still same.

comments.author: yungastronot
comments.body: Easy hack is take a screenshot of a game's UI that you really like, give it to Codex in a project that has your game's context, and tell it to image gen UI for your game inspired by the image without referencing your game's UI. Retry a few times till you get something you like. Play with it. Then give your agent the image with your generated UI and tell it to figure out how to implement this UI into the game 1:1 whatever it takes, no shortcuts. Then you'll have your UI issue done.
